It is probable that this singular proficiency kept his investment of that gentle seclusion unchallenged.

arxiv-2101-09072.title: Lower bounds for the warping degree of a knot projection
arxiv-2101-09072.creator: Atsushi Ohya, Ayaka Shimizu
arxiv-2101-09072.description: Abstract The warping degree of an oriented knot diagram is the minimal number of crossings which we meet as an under-crossing first when we travel along the diagram from a fixed point. The warping degree of a knot projection is the minimal value of the warping degree for all oriented alternating diagrams obtained from the knot projection.

arxiv-2212-05592.title: Modeling halo and central galaxy orientations on the SO(3) manifold with score-based generative models
arxiv-2212-05592.creator: Yesukhei Jagvaral, Rachel Mandelbaum, François Lanusse
arxiv-2212-05592.description: Abstract Upcoming cosmological weak lensing surveys are expected to constrain cosmological parameters with unprecedented precision. In preparation for these surveys, large simulations with realistic galaxy populations are required to test and validate analysis pipelines. However, these simulations are computationally very costly – and at the volumes and resolutions demanded by upcoming cosmological surveys, they are computationally infeasible.

arxiv-2310-15352.title: Rydberg-atom-based single-photon detection for haloscope axion searches
arxiv-2310-15352.creator: Eleanor Graham, Sumita Ghosh, Yuqi Zhu, Xiran Bai, Sidney B. Cahn, Elsa Durcan, Michael J. Jewell, Danielle H. Speller, Sabrina M. Zacarias, Laura T. Zhou, Reina H. Maruyama
arxiv-2310-15352.description: Abstract We propose a Rydberg-atom-based single-photon detector for signal readout in dark matter haloscope experiments between 40 μ \upmu eV and 200 μ \upmu eV (10 GHz and 50 GHz). At these frequencies, standard haloscope readout using linear amplifiers is limited by quantum measurement noise, which can be avoided by using a single-photon detector.

arxiv-2405-10615.title: Cannibals in PARADISE: The effect of merging interplanetary shocks on solar energetic particle events
arxiv-2405-10615.creator: Antonio Niemela, Nicolas Wijsen, Angels Aran, Luciano Rodriguez, Jasmina Magdalenic, Stefaan Poedts
arxiv-2405-10615.description: Abstract Gradual solar energetic particle (SEP) events are associated with shocks driven by coronal mass ejections (CMEs). The merging of two CMEs (so-called Cannibalistic CMEs) and the interaction of their associated shocks, has been linked to some of the most powerful solar storms ever recorded.

arxiv-2412-14970.title: EPOCHS XI: The Structure and Morphology of Galaxies in the Epoch of Reionization to z ∼ 12.5 z\sim 12.5
arxiv-2412-14970.creator: Lewi Westcott, Christopher J. Conselice, Thomas Harvey, Duncan Austin, Nathan Adams, Fabricio Ferrari, Leonardo Ferreira, James Trussler, Qiong Li, Vadim Rusakov, Qiao Duan, Honor Harris, Caio Goolsby, Thomas J. arxiv-2412-14970.description: Abstract We present a structural analysis of 520 galaxy candidates at 6.5 < z < 12.5 6.5<z<12.5 , with SNR > 10 ​ σ >10\sigma in the F444W filter, taken from the EPOCHS v1 sample, consisting of uniformly reduced deep JWST NIRCam data, covering the CEERS, JADES GOOD-S, NGDEEP, SMACS0723, GLASS and PEARLS surveys.

arxiv-2506-17065.title: Flow-Based Non-stationary Temporal Regime Causal Structure Learning
arxiv-2506-17065.creator: Abdellah Rahmani, Pascal Frossard
arxiv-2506-17065.description: Abstract Understanding causal relationships in multivariate time series is crucial in many scenarios, such as those dealing with financial or neurological data. Many such time series exhibit multiple regimes, i.e., consecutive temporal segments with a priori unknown boundaries, with each regime having its own causal structure. Inferring causal dependencies and regime shifts is critical for analyzing the underlying processes.

arxiv-2507-21414.title: Quasinormal modes of regular black holes surrounded by skewed dark matter distributions
arxiv-2507-21414.creator: Chen Lan, Ying-Lei Tian, Hao Yang, Zhen-Xiao Zhang, Yan-Gang Miao
arxiv-2507-21414.description: Abstract Regular black holes, nonsingular solutions to gravitational collapse with quantum corrections, offer a compelling alternative to classical black holes with curvature singularities. In this work, we investigate how the presence of skewed dark matter distributions outside the innermost stable circular orbit of regular black holes modifies the gravitational wave signals emitted by such objects.

pmc-10736578.title: SES DISPARITIES IN FUNCTIONAL IMPAIRMENT WITHIN OLDER ASIAN AMERICANS: COMPARISON OF FOUR RACIAL/ETHNIC GROUPS
pmc-10736578.creator: Katherine Wang, Zheng Zhu, Xiang Qi
pmc-10736578.description: This study investigated to what extent socioeconomic status (SES) disparities associates with functional impairment within older Asians in comparison with other racial/ethnic groups. Data were from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2011-2018 that included 3,297 White, 1,755 Black, 1,708 Hispanic, and 730 Asians aged ≥60.

pmc-11396119.title: Wee1 inhibitor PD0166285 sensitized TP53 mutant lung squamous cell carcinoma to cisplatin via STAT1
pmc-11396119.creator: Qi Li, Wenjie Yang, Qingyi Zhang, Daoming Zhang, Jun Deng, Binxin Chen, Ping Li, Huanqi Zhang, Yiming Jiang, Yangling Li, Bo Zhang, Nengming Lin
pmc-11396119.description: BackgroundLung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSCs) is associated with high mortality (20–30%) and lacks of effective treatments. Almost all LUSC exhibit somatic mutations in TP53. Wee1, a tyrosine kinase, regulates the cell cycle at the G2/M checkpoint. In TP53-deficient cells, the dependence on G2/M checkpoints increases. PD0166285 is the first reported drug with inhibitory activity against both Wee1 and PKMYT1.

pmc-11669895.title: Study on the impact of learning engagement on the subjective wellbeing of empty nesters in rural China
pmc-11669895.creator: Ruirang Zeng, Huiqin Shi, Huiqi Wu, Lixin Sun
pmc-11669895.description: With the rapid development of China's socio-economic landscape and shifts in population structure, rural empty nesters have increasingly become a focal point of social concern. Compared to their urban counterparts, rural empty nesters face more life challenges and psychological stress, making their subjective wellbeing a significant issue.

pmc-12491875.title: Combined opioid-sodium aescinate therapy in blunt thoracic trauma: retrospective evaluation
pmc-12491875.creator: Jun Zhang, Yijie Yan, Zhiyu Guan
pmc-12491875.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundEffective analgesia is crucial for patients with blunt thoracic trauma, yet the optimal analgesic approach remains controversial. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of opioids combined with Sodium Aescinate in blunt thoracic trauma management.MethodsFifty patients with blunt thoracic trauma were randomly assigned to receive either opioids alone (morphine hydrochloride sustained-release tablets (MHST), Group A) or opioids combined with Sodium Aescinate (Group B).

pmc-12667380.title: Barriers and Facilitators to Inhaler Adherence in Elderly Individuals with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Qualitative Study
pmc-12667380.creator: You-Ran Liu, Wenzhong Zhang, Yaqi Huang, Xiulan Peng, Kangming Sun, Zhiying Wu, Huadong Wang, Xiaomei Ji, Jie Wang
pmc-12667380.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundInhalation therapy is the mainstay of pharmacological treatment for patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Elderly individuals with COPD often face greater challenges in using inhalers, and their experiences with inhaler use significantly influence treatment adherence and outcomes.

pmc-13192366.title: Assessing tuberculosis stigma: a pooled multi-country descriptive analysis of 17 high-burden countries using a standardised tool
pmc-13192366.creator: Wai Man Peter Mok, James Malar, Viorel Soltan, Caoimhe Smyth, Kinz Ul Eman, Aris Subakti, Rhea Lobo, Tanaka Mukuhwa, Donald Tobaiwa, Maxime Lunga, Vladyslav Denysenko, Bertille Kayowa, Deliana Garcia, Choub Sok Chamreun
pmc-13192366.description: Tuberculosis (TB) stigma continues to impede equitable access to prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care, undermining efforts to end the epidemic. Despite commitments to eliminate TB stigma in the 2023 United Nations Political Declaration on TB, implementation of evidence-based stigma reduction interventions remains constrained by limited systematic and comparable data.

pmc-13227154.title: Peanut genome resource: a functional genomics platform for Arachis hypogaea
pmc-13227154.creator: Chien-Wen Yang, Chi-Nga Chow, Hua Chen, Kuan-Chieh Tseng, Nai-Yun Wu, Yuhui Zhuang, Weijian Zhuang, Wen-Chi Chang
pmc-13227154.description: Peanut is a vital oilseed legume with considerable nutritional and economic value worldwide. Considering the global agricultural importance of this legume, researchers have sequenced the whole genomes of both wild and cultivated peanut varieties. Furthermore, databases such as PeanutBase have been established to advance peanut research and breeding.

pmc-13318674.title: Rehabilitation Utilization for Parkinson’s Disease in Southern Ghana: A Descriptive Cross‐Sectional Survey
pmc-13318674.creator: Mary Wetani Agoriwo, Marianne Unger, Conran Joseph, Erika Franzén, Suraiya Saleem
pmc-13318674.description: BackgroundThere is limited literature describing rehabilitation utilization among the Parkinson’s disease (PD) population across the world and especially in Africa, despite ample evidence and clinical guidelines in support of rehabilitation for persons with PD (PwPD).ObjectivesTo describe the characteristics of PwPD, the types of rehabilitation services and treatment parameters used, and the factors associated with rehabilitation utilization in southern Ghana.

pmc-13361601.title: Ultrasonographic Knee Abnormalities and Their Association with Pain in Young Male Handball and Basketball Athletes: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-13361601.creator: Nicoleta Anamaria Pascalau, Alexandru Bogdan Ilieș, Brigitte Osser, Csongor Toth, Gyongyi Osser, Laura Ioana Bondar, Gheorghe Codruț Bulz, Anca Maria Sabău, Mihaela Gavrila-Ardelean, Corina Dalia Toderescu
pmc-13361601.description: Background/Objectives: Knee injuries and overuse-related disorders are common among athletes participating in jumping sports such as handball and basketball. Musculoskeletal ultrasonography is increasingly used for the assessment of knee pathology; however, evidence regarding the prevalence and clinical relevance of ultrasonographic abnormalities in young athletes remains limited.

pmc-13433427.title: Editorial: Advances in neuromodulation for chronic pain: mechanisms and clinical implications
pmc-13433427.creator: Hong Jiang, Linlin Sun, Fengyu Liu, Hong Jiang
pmc-13433427.description: roinflammation, impaired descending inhibition, and affective-cognitive modulation together contribute to the transition from acute to chronic pain. These mechanisms help explain why conventional pharmacological approaches often provide incomplete relief, are limited by adverse effects, and may fail to address the neural processes that sustain pain chronicity.

pmc-13562215.title: The paddle effect on speed perception: A multilevel Bayesian meta-analysis
pmc-13562215.creator: Wenbo Luo, Lunbo Zhang, Yuki Yamada
pmc-13562215.description: The paddle effect is considered one of the most robust phenomena in action-specific perception. In computer game-based Pong tasks, participants perceive targets as moving more slowly when using a larger paddle compared to a smaller one. We employed multilevel Bayesian modeling to conduct the first meta-analysis of this literature.

pmc-13616204.title: Screening GGC repeat expansion in the NOTCH2NLC in early‐onset dementia: The Longitudinal Study of Early Onset Dementia and Family Members (LEAF) Study
pmc-13616204.creator: Seung‐yeon Lee, Takeshi Mizuguchi, Hee Jin Kim, Young‐Eun Kim, Cho Hanna, Won‐Joo Kim, Gha‐Hyun Lee, Ahro Kim, Ji‐Yun Park, Eun Joo Chung, Hyemin Jang, Na‐Yeon Jung, Sun Min Lee, Sang Won Seo, Seong‐Ho Koh, Henrik Zetterberg, Liana G. Apostolova, Naomichi Matsumoto, So Young Moon, Eun‐Joo Kim, the L
pmc-13616204.description: BACKGROUNDNeuronal intranuclear inclusion disease (NIID) is neurodegenerative disorder caused by GGC repeat expansion in NOTCH2NLC. Given its frequency in young East Asian adults and overlap with cognitive impairment in young adults, a key feature of early‐onset dementia (EOD), we screened NOTCH2NLC GGC repeat expansions in Korean patients with EOD.
